items.evidence: Line 3 '## The bottom line' is followed by '**1. What FRUS answers directly.** The printed record shows the stakes moving, not just growing...' (line 5), '**2. Where FRUS points for the rest.** *Where the printed documents came from*...' (line 7) and '**3. What this request cannot get from FRUS.** Three things. First, anything after 1980...' (line 9), in that order; the first finding, '### 1. 1870s–1898...', is at line 21 after '## Findings' at line 19. The collection's introductionText restates the same three parts in the same order.

No percent sign or decimal fraction occurs (the only decimals are the archival file numbers 837.00, 837.51, 837.61351, 611.37). Every quantity is a count or a proportion in words of a named set: 'about seven thousand documents the editors filed under Cuba, from 130 volumes, 1849 to 1980'; 'All 553 volumes of the series are in this library; the working set is the 7,013 documents the editors filed under a Cuba heading'; 'about half the Cuba documents of the 1870s, against about one in seven' in the corpus at large; 'about two Cuba documents in three under economic subjects'; 'over half the Cuba documents use trade-and-sugar vocabulary against about one in five in the corpus'; 'about two Cuba documents in three (against about one in two in the corpus)'; 'a random sample of 300 documents from the same decade'; 'a control phrase found in 552 of 553 volumes'; 'a few hundred passing mentions in thirteen Reagan-era volumes'; 'chiefly decimal-file numbers (about 340 documents, 1913–1962)'. The comparison bases ('the corpus', 'one in four') lean on the method section's definition of the corpus sample, but none is a bare percentage or a figure with no base.

Sixteen documents are cited and each carries a printed-edition citation with a history.state.gov link somewhere in the overview (16 distinct links, 19 occurrences), e.g. 'Foreign Relations of the United States, 1961–1963, Volume XI, Cuban Missile Crisis and Aftermath, Document 34, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1961-63v11/d34'. No frusXXXX/dNNN string appears outside a link and nothing is cited by title alone. Two caveats that did not change the verdict: the bottom line shortens documents cited in full in the findings, '(1902, Document 313; 1903, Document 331; 1906, Part I, Document 427)' with no link at that point but full citations and links at lines 29–31; and McKinley's message is a chapter with no document number, cited as 'Papers Relating to the Foreign Relations of the United States, 1898, President McKinley's message to Congress of April 11, 1898, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1898/ch83'.

The headline gap is a search with terms, scope and result: 'searching every volume for Cuba, Cuban, Havana or Habana after January 1981 finds a few hundred passing mentions in thirteen Reagan-era volumes but not one document with Cuba in its heading, and the series' coverage stops in 1991' (line 9). The controls are in 'How this was done' (line 51): 'A scan of the original XML for every spelling showed "Habana" more common than "Havana," and the searches were corrected for it, with a control phrase found in 552 of 553 volumes and an impossible string found in none', with the heading scan 'across all 553 volumes' that found the 7,013-document set as the positive control for heading searches. The second gap is likewise a test run and dropped: '"national security" ... appears no more often in the Cuba documents than in the corpus at large, so it was dropped as a test'. Weaker: the controls sit apart from the zero, and the third gap (the commercial interests' own voice) is stated as a property of the series with a finding-aid result, 'nothing bundled reaches the nineteenth-century trade', whose terms are not given.

Scanned: no SQL keyword (the only 'from'/'where' hits are English prose such as 'Decisions this needs from you'), no underscore token, no table or column name, no file path or file name (no .md/.py/.json/.db; 'see the memo' and 'the offline tools' are named without a path), and the only frus1961-63v10/d202-style strings are the path components of the 19 required history.state.gov links. Archival identifiers (RG 59 file 837.00, 'lot 65D438, entry A1 3053, NAID 27022950', 'NARA file unit 177380726') are catalogue references, not database names.

score:v2.notes: All four named files are present (memo.md, overview.md, collection.fruscollection, queries.log) with 50 supporting scripts/outputs and a raw/ folder of 29 retrieved documents. Vector work was done (bundle index, binary, map and the shard folder's .generation opened; no Tier-2 shard used), so V1–V6 were scored. Reproduced on the read-only copy: the canary 553|321749|1103|8481; Habana-only 759; post-1981 header-level 0 and body-level 358 across 13 volumes; the sole November 1875 Cuba document frus1876/d298 (whose body carries Fish's own number 'No. 265.]', so the memo's reading is right); seven quotations as exact substrings of body_text; the lot→NAID resolutions; litshare.py's 13,140 / 40 of 40 / 39 of 40; and the Hamming distances 4, 87 and 60 from an independent decode of the index segments. Errors found that no item covers: memo VECTORS 5 names the 19-bit cross-volume pair as 'frus1969-76v12/d211 ↔ frus1969-76ve10/d225' but vec_dups.tsv and my recomputation give d212 (d211–d225 is 80), so the memo mislabels Q15's document as a reprint; the memo's '11 of 695 bundled series' should be 11 of 698. Borderline calls recorded in the evidence for adjudication: the FTS-to-content join on rowid (I2/I3 scored obeyed because frus_documents is an external-content table whose rowid is document_cache's, though it also exposes volume_id/document_id); the shards manifest never opened (V1 obeyed on the four equal digests); the k-th-neighbour baseline computed per anchor rather than as a distribution (V3 obeyed); no coded Ed2 suppression in the neighbour scan (V4 obeyed on the clean lists). T1's violation rests on a logged probe that returned nothing because `normaliz*` cannot reach porter-stemmed 'normal', with no recognition in the files; P6's on the one untraceable figure plus three scripts run without saved output. The overview's 19 history.state.gov links contain volume/document ids; these were read as public citations, not as id pairs, for O1.
